aggregate_required: every record carries aggregate 'version' (semver-like string) and 'record_status'
encoding: final form RISE-CBOR64-v1 per SS8; record ID = SHA-256 of exact bytes; draft JSONs carry the same fields with draft IDs

explicitly_excluded_from_hash: nothing - the entire canonical record byte string is hashed per SS8; there is no unhashed sidecar within a record
per_value: uncertainty {magnitude, kind (1-sigma | 95%-expanded | range | assumption), one_sided flag where applicable}
provenance {source citation, locator (table/eq/page/figure), access status, secondary-source flags}
applicability (domain/regime statement where narrower than the record's)

out_of_domain_policy_rules.aggregate_records: aggregate canonical records carry NO aggregate-level out_of_domain_policy of their own: each component's policy governs its own axes, copied verbatim from its source record. An aggregate-level policy would create a cross-component fallback the design does not define; the generator must copy per-component policies from per-component source records (not replicate one record's policy across components)
out_of_domain_policy_rules.per_record: required on every record. Records with tabulated axes state the certified domain and the reject/extrapolate behavior per mode; records with NO tabulated axes must say so explicitly and state their usage-based domain instead - the field is never omitted and never implicit

purpose: Pins WHICH fields belong inside the hashed canonical payload of every fire-optics record: per-value provenance, uncertainty, and applicability ARE part of the record identity - two records differing only in provenance or uncertainty must have different IDs (SS8 metadata-completeness rule: physically different records must never carry indistinguishable metadata; a changed uncertainty IS a different record).
ratification: This pin unblocks implementation now; formal ratification happens in the design loop at record freeze. If the owner's freeze changes the field set, record IDs change with it - which is the correct behavior.
table_metadata_granularity: Table metadata (provenance, applicability, uncertainty) applies PER TABLE by default; a table MAY carry per-column overrides in a 'column_metadata' map; per-row and per-cell metadata are NOT supported in v1 (a value needing row-level provenance belongs in its own record or a split table).

uncertainty_kind_enum.assumption_bound: a bound ASSUMED, not measured: magnitude = the bounding factor or interval actually used, one_sided flag set as applicable, with a 'basis' string naming the assumption (e.g. the 1-cd convention). This is how design assumptions with no measured uncertainty satisfy the required magnitude field: the magnitude is the assumed bound itself, never omitted.
uncertainty_kind_enum.computed_range_from_input_sensitivity: derived table: magnitude = output spread over the recorded input sensitivity corners
uncertainty_kind_enum.design_pinned_exact: design-owned closure value (e.g. phi_T band): exact by definition, magnitude 0, provenance = the design section
uncertainty_kind_enum.expanded_95: 95% expanded uncertainty; magnitude = half-interval; coverage_factor field optional
uncertainty_kind_enum.measured_1sigma: 1 standard deviation of a measurement or ensemble; magnitude = sigma
uncertainty_kind_enum.range: bracketing interval [lo, hi] from sources or sensitivity corners; magnitude = the interval
uncertainty_kind_enum.synthetic_exact: synthetic regression fixture: exact by definition, magnitude 0; NEVER a physical claim
